"When there comes the help of God" [i.e., the support of God granted to His Prophet (ﷺ)] over his enemies, "and the victory" [i.e., the conquest of Makkah].

﴿And you see the people entering the religion of God﴾, i.e., Islam, ﴿in multitudes﴾, groups, after it had been that one by one would enter it. This was after the conquest of Mecca; the Arabs came to him from the regions of the earth, submitting willingly.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 110, verse 3:

﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise﴾, meaning, while being clothed in His praise, ﴿and seek His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾. After the revelation of this surah, the Prophet (ﷺ) used to frequently say: "Subhan Allah wa bihamdih, astaghfir Allah wa atubu ilayh" (Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; I seek the forgiveness of Allah and turn to Him in repentance). Through it, he knew that his death had drawn near. The conquest of Makkah took place in Ramadan of the eighth year (of the Hijrah), and the Prophet (ﷺ) passed away in Rabi' al-Awwal of the tenth year.
